reviews.one_line_contribution: The claim that a retrieved memory item's marginal value is a property of the (item, instruction) pair rather than of the item, operationalized as a unit-level REDUNDANT/NOVEL/CONFLICTING labeling against the task instruction, and tested by token-matched surgical deletion with a decoy-instruction placebo plus a novel-units-per-token retrieval rule.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two clusters. (a) For the phenomenon, the ACL 2026 experience-following study the proposal itself names: it already establishes helps/hurts/low-value under similarity retrieval, so this proposal owns only the mechanism, and it correctly concedes that. (b) The more dangerous cluster is one the proposal never checks: query-conditioned context compression and instruction-conditioned retrieval. RECOMP (Xu et al. 2023), LLMLingua-2 and Provence-style pruners already delete context spans that the conditioning text makes unnecessary, at sub-item granularity, at matched token budgets; Promptriever/FollowIR/INSTRUCTOR already condition retrieval scoring on an instruction string rather than the bare query. Swapping the conditioning text from 'query' to 'agent instruction' and the objective from 'relevance' to 'non-entailment' is a small, natural delta on top of that machinery, and a reviewer who knows that literature will read Part 3 as instruction-conditioned RECOMP applied to a memory bank. Sufficient Context (ICLR 2025) supplies the conceptual frame ('does the context add what is missing') and the proposal's own defense — that 'missing' there is relative to question plus parametric knowledge — is thin, because parametric knowledge is exactly the analogue of 'what the prompt already says'.
reviews.strongest_objection: Part 1, the predictive core, is powered as if it had 1,000 balanced binary observations, but its outcomes (fix and break of S1 vs S0) are rare events whose rate the design only bounds from below at 6% movement in *either* direction (precheck, 150 dev instances). This track's own prior result was a bank that fixed zero items and broke six to seven. So a bank that passes the gate entirely on breaks yields literally zero fix events, and prediction 2's 'novel-unit count predicts fixes' becomes untestable while the study proceeds. Even in a favorable case, 6-10% total movement over 500 instances x 2 conditions gives on the order of 20-40 fix events and a similar number of breaks, against a mixed-effects logistic model carrying seven fixed effects (three unit counts, injected tokens, retrieval score, instance difficulty, embedding proxy) plus instance random effects. That is roughly 3-5 events per variable, an order of magnitude short of what the stated 0.22 standardized-log-odds detection assumes, and the 'removing the three unit counts drops explained deviance by 25% relative' test is essentially unconstrained at that event count. The conflicting channel is worse: no expected prevalence of CONFLICTING units is stated anywhere, the 400-pair validation set will likely contain very few of them (so the kappa>0.6 gate can pass while the CONFLICTING class is unvalidated), and S5 (drop-conflicting) was cut, so the break half of the mechanism -- the half that matters most given the track's headline harm result -- has no causal arm and an unpowered regression coefficient. Secondary but nearly as damaging: the I_short/I_long manipulation that carries prediction 1 is confounded three ways. I_long is simultaneously (i) more redundant with the bank, (ii) more accurate on this task distribution, hence lower headroom for memory to fix anything, and (iii) longer, which by the proposal's own cited Context Length Alone Hurts should depress performance independent of content. A collapse in S1-S0 from I_short to I_long is exactly what a pure ceiling/headroom account predicts with no unit-level mechanism, and baseline (iv) is explicitly counted as confirmation rather than as the rival explanation it is. Third: predictions 1 and 5 are in tension. Prediction 1 says memory's gain collapses under I_long; Part 3 is run under I_long only and prediction 5 demands complementarity beat top-k by >=5 points there. If S1-S0 under I_long is near zero, no reallocation of which items get injected can move accuracy 5 points unless top-k is actively harmful under I_long by several points, which is neither predicted nor powered. Fourth, an arithmetic inconsistency: prediction 1 caps REDUNDANT at <=15% of units under I_short, so S2 can delete at most ~15% of tokens there, yet prediction 3 asserts S2 cuts injected tokens by >=40% while being equivalent to S1 'pooled across instruction conditions'. Pooling a condition where S2 is a near-no-op by construction into an equivalence test biases straight toward declaring equivalence, and the same pooling makes the token-savings headline unachievable as stated.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Compute Part 1's power on the fix and break event counts, not on 1,000 instances, and make the precheck gate the *fix* rate specifically (e.g. >=8% of dev instances fixed under at least one instruction) rather than movement in either direction; if fixes cannot be made numerous enough, drop the seven-regressor model for a pre-registered two- or three-term model and state the CONFLICTING prevalence you expect, oversampling conflicting pairs into the 400-pair validation set so that class is actually validated. (2) Add a third instruction condition that breaks the confound: an I_long_control matched to I_long in length, register and (as far as possible) no-memory accuracy but produced so that its content does not overlap the bank -- e.g. optimized on a disjoint training slice or on a different guidance axis. Relationality is only established if the same items go redundant under I_long and stay novel under I_long_control while the S1-S0 gain drops only in the former. Without this, the S7 decoy controls the deletion arms but nothing controls the manipulation that prediction 1 rests on. (3) Restore an S5-type drop-conflicting arm, or accept and state that the break/CONFLICTING branch is descriptive only and remove it from the headline three-way claim. (4) Report the S2-vs-S1 equivalence and the token-savings figure per instruction condition, never pooled. (5) Move at least one Part 3 budget to I_short, or state and power the specific mechanism by which complementarity wins under I_long (avoided harm, not added fixes), and report the S1-S0 ceiling alongside every rule comparison so the reader can see how much room any rule had.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First and most important, the length- and headroom-matched control instruction described above -- the proposal has an instruction-level placebo nowhere, only a deletion-level one (S7), so the single manipulation carrying the central relationality claim is uncontrolled. Second, a single-call LLM instruction-conditioned pruner: put the instruction and the top-k items in one frontier-or-local model call and ask it to delete what the instruction already says, at the same token budget as S2/complementarity. The proposal cut LLM-compressor baselines on the grounds that MMR tests the same thing more cleanly, which is wrong -- MMR is item-vs-item and tests the reference-set claim, while the LLM pruner is instruction-conditioned and tests the *instrument* claim from the strong side. As written, the instrument is defended only against a deliberately weak competitor (embedding cosine plus Jaccard); a reviewer will note that the interesting question is whether atomic decomposition plus DeBERTa-MNLI beats one prompt, and that question is not asked. A third, cheaper omission: appending the NOVEL units directly to the instruction instead of injecting items, which is the natural test of risk factor 4 (does guidance need episodic form) and would cost one extra arm.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average for this kind of check and clearly a real search, with an honest OpenReview caveat and a correct concession that the ACL 2026 experience-following paper removes the right to claim the phenomenon. But it is scoped to one niche -- agent-memory harm -- and therefore misses the literature where the actual method already lives. It contains no search of context/prompt compression (RECOMP, LLMLingua/LLMLingua-2, Provence and their 2026 successors), which does conditioned sub-item deletion at matched token budgets, and none of instruction-conditioned retrieval (Promptriever, FollowIR, INSTRUCTOR and follow-ups), which already scores candidates against an instruction string rather than a query. Instruction-conditioned redundancy pruning of a memory bank sits directly between those two lines, and the proposal's own predicted failure mode -- the cheap embedding-overlap proxy wins -- is precisely the result that compression work would lead you to expect. The proposal's stated risk that 'instruction-aware dedup appears as an appendix ablation in a contemporaneous context-compilation preprint' is, in my judgment, understated rather than nontrivial. Separately, four of the seven cited items are arXiv identifiers I cannot verify (2601.07470, 2605.09330, 2606.19847, 2607.05936); I do not treat that as bad faith, but a submission version should carry titles plus venues and the authors should confirm those IDs resolve, since a check whose load-bearing citations cannot be resolved by a reviewer establishes less novelty than it appears to. Net: not a collision I can name, but the check is under-scoped in the direction that matters most, so it does not fully discharge the novelty burden.

reviews.one_line_contribution: The claim that an injected memory item's marginal value is a property of the (item, instruction) pair rather than of the item — operationalized by decomposing both the task instruction and each retrieved item into atomic guidance units and labeling each item unit against the instruction as REDUNDANT/NOVEL/CONFLICTING with an off-the-shelf NLI model — together with a per-instance token-matched surgical ablation (drop-redundant vs drop-random vs drop-novel vs decoy-instruction placebo) and a retrieval rule scoring candidates by instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per token.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The authors name Sufficient Context (ICLR 2025) and AtomMem as the threats, and they are right that neither uses the instruction as the reference set. The threat they never mention is the query/instruction-conditioned context- and prompt-compression line — LongLLMLingua / LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, Provence and the 2026 context-curation/context-engineering successors. Those systems already prune retrieved context conditioned on the full prompt (which contains the instruction), and their headline result is exactly this proposal's headline deliverable: roughly half the injected tokens at preserved accuracy, beating token-matched random or naive truncation. That literature does not decompose the *instruction* into guidance units, does not produce a three-way taxonomy, and does not run a decoy-instruction placebo, so it does not fully collide — but it makes the practical contribution (S2 and Part 3) look like a re-derivation with heavier machinery, and it is absent from Related Work entirely. Secondary threats the proposal also does not engage: ExpeL's own insight-vs-demonstration split (the instruction/memory division of labour is the framing ExpeL already operates under), and the context-memory knowledge-conflict literature (e.g. Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth and successors), which is the established home of the CONFLICTING channel and has already characterized when contextual guidance that contradicts what the model was told is followed or ignored.
reviews.strongest_objection: Prediction 1 — the relationality claim the title rests on — is confounded, and it is the one claim with no placebo. I_short and I_long differ in two things at once: content overlap with the memory bank, and the fact that I_long is a GEPA-optimized instruction that independently raises accuracy and lengthens the prompt. Any two independently helpful interventions are generically sub-additive, so S1−S0 shrinking by ≥5 points from I_short to I_long is predicted by ceiling/base-rate mechanics with no reference to unit-level redundancy: under I_long, S0 is higher, so fewer instances remain fixable and more remain breakable, and the paired fix/break table is measured against a different base rate. The proposal built a decoy instruction (S7) precisely to remove the identity of the conditioning text in Part 2, then failed to build the analogous control for Part 1 — there is no length-, register- and optimizer-matched instruction whose content does *not* overlap the bank. As written, the label-distribution shift (≤15% → ≥40% REDUNDANT) and the gain collapse can both occur while the causal story is false. A second, independent problem: the precheck gate requires only that the bank move ≥6% of dev instances 'in either direction', which admits exactly the regime this research track already measured — a bank that fixes zero items and breaks six or seven. In that regime Part 1's fix regression on novel-unit count and prediction 3's clause that S4 'loses ≥5 points of fixes relative to S2' have almost no events to model, and half the paper is unpowered while the precheck reports green. Third, and smaller: S3 (token-matched random deletion) is not an independent control but a diluted S4 — a random subset deletes novel units in proportion, so S2 > S3 follows from S4 hurting, and the only genuinely non-tautological arm is S7, whose construction is under-specified. Under a decoy instruction almost every item unit should label NOVEL, so the decoy-REDUNDANT set will typically be far smaller than the real one, and the proposal never says how S7 is padded to per-instance token match; if it is padded at random, S7 degenerates into S3 and prediction 4 ('S7 recovers less than half of the S2−S3 gap') becomes a statement about the padding rule rather than about instruction identity.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an I_long_control arm: an instruction matched to I_long in length, register and optimizer provenance (e.g. GEPA run on a disjoint training split or against a different objective) whose guidance content is largely disjoint from the frozen bank, and pre-register that the redundancy shift and the gain collapse appear for I_long but not I_long_control. Without this the relationality claim cannot be separated from sub-additivity, and it is cheap — one extra optimizer run plus S0/S1 at 500×2. (2) Report fixes and breaks as separate outcomes with base-rate-adjusted contrasts across instruction conditions rather than leaning on net paired deltas whose base rates differ by construction. (3) Tighten the precheck to gate on fix *events* specifically (e.g. ≥25 fixes under at least one instruction), not total movement, since the novel-unit→fix channel is untestable in a fix-free bank and this track has already observed one. (4) Specify S7's token-matching rule exactly and pre-register it — how the decoy-redundant set is extended when it is smaller than the real one — or replace S7 with a shuffled-instruction-assignment placebo (label item units against a *different real instance's* optimized instruction) where the label set is naturally comparable in size. (5) Add an instruction-conditioned compression baseline (below). (6) Budget full-scale LLM labeling as the fallback instrument (~400 items × ~5 units × 2 instructions is well under the stated $100 headroom) so that an NLI–human kappa below 0.6 downgrades the instrument rather than terminating the study; as written, only 400 validation pairs have LLM labels, and DeBERTa-MNLI is out of distribution on imperative-vs-imperative pairs where 'redundant' means near-paraphrase, not entailment. (7) Reconcile the internal inconsistency: the Abstract/Short Hypothesis promise '~half the injected tokens' from dropping redundant units, but prediction 1 sets redundancy at ≤15% of units under I_short and ≥40% under I_long, and unit share is not token share once per-item boilerplate survives deletion. Report realized token savings per instruction condition and scope the equivalence claim to I_long.
reviews.missing_baseline: An instruction-conditioned context/prompt-compression baseline at matched injected-token budget — LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, or even a small extractive sentence-selector scoring each item sentence against the instruction — run both as a Part 3 selection/compression rule and as a Part 1 competing regressor. This is the 'LLM-compressor baseline' the proposal explicitly cut, and the stated reason for cutting it is wrong: the justification says MMR tests item-level curation more cleanly, but a compressor conditioned on the instruction is not item-level curation at all — it is the instruction-as-reference-set hypothesis implemented without atomic decomposition, i.e. the single strongest competitor to both the instrument claim and the method claim, and the thing a practitioner would actually deploy. The embedding/lexical overlap proxy is a weaker stand-in and does not cover it. Secondary omissions: (a) the length/optimizer-matched control instruction described above, which is a missing arm rather than a missing method; (b) an instruction-augmentation arm that appends the bank's NOVEL units to the instruction instead of injecting them as retrieved items, which is the direct test of the proposal's own Risk #4 (that guidance must be restated in concrete episodic form to be followed) and is the natural 'why retrieve at all' baseline for a paper whose thesis is that only the novel units carry value.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is more diligent than most: seven named items, a per-item collide/does-not-collide verdict, an explicit retraction of a citation cluster (SkillZip/SkillRAE/SkillOps) the current search failed to reconfirm, and a stated caveat about unindexed OpenReview 2026 submissions with a self-assessed nontrivial collision risk. That is genuine work and I credit it. But it searched the wrong neighbourhood for the contribution it is defending. Every one of the seven items sits in the agent-memory-harm niche; nothing in the search covers prompt or context compression, instruction-aware context pruning, or the 2026 context-engineering/context-curation line, which is precisely where a preprint claiming 'condition pruning on what the prompt already says, cut half the injected tokens at matched accuracy' would appear — and that is the proposal's operational deliverable, not a side result. Nothing covers the context-memory knowledge-conflict literature either, which already studies the CONFLICTING channel under a different name. So the concluding paragraph ('no located work decomposes both the agent instruction and each retrieved memory item into guidance units') is true but weak evidence, because the searches run could not have located such work. I cannot name a specific recent preprint that makes the exact (item unit, instruction unit) marginal-value claim, so I do not treat this as scooped; I do treat the check as establishing novelty for the framing while leaving novelty for the instrument and the method unestablished. The authors' own estimate — that instruction-aware dedup plausibly already exists as an appendix ablation in a contemporaneous context-compilation preprint — strikes me as accurate and, given the missing compression baseline, more damaging than they allow.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That a retrieved memory item's marginal value is a property of the (item, instruction) pair rather than of the item — operationalized by splitting both texts into atomic guidance units and labeling each item unit against the instruction as redundant/novel/conflicting — together with a token-matched unit-level surgical ablation, a decoy-instruction placebo, and a retrieval rule that maximizes instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per token.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The cluster the proposal never cites: prompt/context compression conditioned on the surrounding prompt — LongLLMLingua and LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, Selective Context, Provence, CompAct. Those systems already delete spans of retrieved context that add nothing given the rest of the prompt, at matched token budgets, and report exactly the headline result of Prediction 3 (accuracy preserved at roughly half the injected tokens). The proposal's defense would be that they condition on the query while it conditions on the instruction, but in an agent scaffold the instruction is simply part of the conditioning prompt those compressors already see, so the delta is a choice of reference span rather than a new mechanism. Sufficient Context (cited) is the conceptual predecessor and AtomMem (cited) supplies the entailment-dedup machinery; between them plus the compression literature, what remains genuinely new is the two-instruction relationality manipulation and the decoy placebo, not the redundant/novel/conflicting axis itself. The Related Work section's failure to engage compression at all reads, to a skeptical AC, as the novelty case not having been tested where the idea actually lives.
reviews.strongest_objection: The entire Part 2/Part 3 prediction set presupposes a memory bank with several points of exploitable net effect, and the design does not guarantee one. The track's own prior measurement in this setup is 0 fixes and 6-7 breaks — net effect near zero or slightly negative — and the precheck gate only requires the bank to move >=6% of dev instances 'in either direction', which is churn, not gain. If S1-S0 is ~0 under both instructions (the modal outcome given that prior result), then S2, S3, S4 and S7 are all interventions on an intervention that did nothing: 'S3 loses >=5 points relative to S2' and 'S4 loses >=5 points of fixes relative to S2' are arithmetically near-impossible when there are not 5 points of memory-derived accuracy in the system to remove, and the honest report becomes a bundle of 'inconclusive' rows that the proposal pre-labels a 'clean negative supporting the budget account'. That is not a publishable negative; it is a null about a taxonomy that was never given anything to explain. Second, and independently: Prediction 1 (relationality) is confounded. I_long differs from I_short in content overlap with the bank AND in length AND in baseline accuracy — a GEPA-optimized instruction raises S0, shrinking the fixable set, so a >=5-point collapse in paired gain S1-S0 is precisely what a headroom/ceiling account predicts with zero relationality. The decoy instruction, which is the right control for this, is spent in S7 on the surgery arm and never used as a third instruction condition where it is actually needed. Third, the manipulation has n=1 instruction per condition (one optimizer run, one hand-written prompt); every McNemar test treats instances as the unit while the treatment of interest is the instruction, so no inference generalizes over instructions. The 3-seed optimizer sweep that was cut for budget was the only replication of the study's central manipulation. Fourth, the redundancy is manufactured: I_long is optimized on the same 300 training instances the ExpeL bank is written from, so the label-distribution half of Prediction 1 is close to tautological and the Part 3 method operates in a redundancy regime engineered by shared provenance rather than one that occurs in deployment.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a third instruction condition I_decoy_long — length-, register- and token-matched to I_long but optimized on a disjoint split or task so it cannot absorb bank content — and restate Prediction 1 as a difference-in-differences: the gain drop under I_long minus the gain drop under I_decoy_long. Without this the relationality claim is not separable from length and ceiling effects. (2) Produce I_long from >=3 optimizer seeds so the instruction is a replicated unit; report the between-instruction variance rather than treating a single optimizer output as a condition. (3) Re-gate the precheck on net paired effect, not churn: require |S1-S0| >= the stated MDE under at least one instruction before spending 20k episodes, and pre-register what is reported if the bank is inert. (4) Add an off-the-shelf instruction-conditioned compressor and a per-instance oracle subset as the two endpoints for S2 and for Part 3, so the reader can see how much of the achievable headroom the taxonomy captures. (5) Build I_long from a split disjoint from the bank's write split, so redundancy is discovered rather than constructed. (6) Estimate instance difficulty from seeds held out of the S0 arm used for pairing; as written, difficulty is derived from the same S0 runs that define the fix/break outcome, which mechanically correlates the regressor with the response. (7) State an inter-human kappa floor alongside the NLI-human >0.6 gate — 'redundant' between imperative guidance units is a construct humans may not agree on, and NLI-human agreement cannot exceed what inter-human agreement permits; DeBERTa-MNLI is also out of distribution on imperatives, where general instructions fail to entail specific heuristics that are nonetheless behaviorally redundant.
reviews.missing_baseline: An off-the-shelf prompt/context compressor applied to the retrieved items with the instruction as conditioning context, at matched injected-token budget (LongLLMLingua / LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, or Provence). This is the deployed alternative to S2 and to the Part 3 selection rule, it is cheap to run, and it is absent from both the baseline list and the related work — the cheap embedding-overlap proxy is not a substitute, since a reviewer's question is not 'does a cheaper feature work' but 'does an existing compressor already do this'. Also missing: a per-instance oracle best-subset upper bound, without which a null in Part 3 cannot be distinguished from 'there was nothing to select'.
reviews.preprint_collision: Unusually specific for a collision check — seven named items, explicit verdicts, and an honest caveat about unindexed OpenReview 2026 — and it correctly identifies that the ACL 2026 experience-following study removes the right to claim the phenomenon. Two problems. First, it searched only the agent-memory-harm niche and reports nothing from the neighborhoods where the idea actually lives: context/prompt compression (LLMLingua family, RECOMP, Provence, CompAct), retrieval-vs-parametric-knowledge gating (Adaptive-RAG, self-knowledge-guided retrieval, 'when not to retrieve'), and the knowledge-conflict literature — the CONFLICTING channel is context-memory knowledge conflict under a new name, and not one paper from that line is cited. A search that covers only the area where you expect to be safe has not established novelty. Second, the check itself discloses that the skill-library dedup citations in the previous draft (SkillZip / SkillRAE / SkillOps) 'was not re-confirmed by this search' — i.e., an earlier version of this proposal cited work that may not exist. That materially lowers confidence in the unverifiable arXiv identifiers carried here (2605.09330, 2606.19847, 2601.07470, 2607.05936); each should be verified by title and abstract in the paper, and the collision check should state which were retrieved versus recalled. I did not find a preprint making this exact claim, but on the evidence presented the search is not broad enough for the proposal's novelty claim to be taken as established.
